metadata.note: Amtrak stations, generated by stationpull.py from https://content.amtrak.com/content/gtfs/GTFS.zip. Each station carries a services[] entry per route calling there, with a real count of trips that stop at this station on this route -- not a route-wide headway, so an express that passes through does not inflate it. Departure times live in the per-route files under data/timetables/, referenced by each service.
metadata.not_yet_sourced: A service dated 2026-2026 has no published timetable evidence behind it yet and claims only what the feed proves; one starting earlier names the timetables it was found in. Nothing before 2008 is covered: Amtrak published its last system timetable in June 2018, and earlier years exist only as scanned images at timetables.org, which would need OCR. Nothing covers 2019-2025 either. Where a service does start earlier, the departure count, destinations and linked timetable still describe 2026 alone -- the older timetables establish that the train stopped, not how often.
metadata.line_geometry_gaps: 0 stop/route pairs sit more than 2.0 km from the line feature carrying their service, and say so in their own sources. Every one is a branch that data/amtrak.geojson does not draw, because it uses a single representative GTFS shape per route: Northeast Regional up the Springfield Line and into Virginia, the Texas Eagle west of San Antonio, the Pacific Surfliner north of Los Angeles, the Capitol Corridor beyond Oakland, the Empire Builder past Spokane. The stations are correct; the drawn routes are incomplete.
